beats.label: S1 · A hitman finds a class
beats.text: Hitman Barry arrives in LA to kill actor Ryan on a Chechen contract, tails him into Gene Cousineau's acting class, and glimpses a life he wants instead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the show's core tension — the hit that pulls Barry into the world he can't leave.

beats.label: S1 · Barry Block is born
beats.text: Ryan is killed by the Chechens before Barry can act; Barry shoots them but is caught on a lipstick camera, and joins Gene's class as 'Barry Block'.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Creates both the police thread (camera evidence) and Barry's double-life alias driving every subsequent season.

beats.label: S1 · The airfield goes wrong
beats.text: Pressured into more hits, Barry strangles Paco and helps his old marine friend Chris raid a Bolivian airfield, where fellow marines Taylor and Vaughn are shot dead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Escalates Barry's killing and produces the surviving witness — Chris — whose fate is the season's moral pivot.

beats.label: S1 · Barry kills his friend
beats.text: Fellow marine Chris survives the raid and vows to confess to police; Barry kills him, stages a suicide, and breaks down onstage the same night.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The first innocent Barry chooses to kill — and the trauma that fuels every later 'stop killing' promise he'll break.

beats.label: S1 · Hank takes the throne
beats.text: Learning the Chechens plan to kill Fuches, Barry storms Goran's house, kills Goran, and drives Fuches out of LA; Hank takes over, allied with the Bolivians.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resets the gang board Barry will orbit next season — Hank in charge, Fuches exiled and dangerous.

beats.label: S1 · Moss connects the dots
beats.text: Detective Janice Moss, now dating Gene, pieces together Barry's link to Chris and Taylor on Facebook at Gene's cabin and refuses to let it drop.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The realisation that forces Barry's most consequential kill — and the death that haunts every season after.

beats.label: S1 · Shots at the cabin
beats.text: Barry retrieves a hidden gun and shoots Moss dead at Gene's cabin, then returns to sleeping Sally and tells himself, once again, that his criminal life is over.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The murder that becomes the show's central buried secret — the one Gene, Fuches and Jim Moss all chase next.

cliffhanger.text: Detective Moss lies dead at Gene's cabin, Sally sleeps unaware, and Barry once again declares his killing life over — while Gene has just heard the shots that changed everything.
questions: Will Gene realise Barry killed the woman he was falling for?
Can Barry actually stay out with Fuches gone and Hank in charge?
What does Hank's new alliance with the Bolivians mean for Barry?

characters.name: Barry Berkman
characters.line: Marine-turned-hitman trying to reinvent as actor 'Barry Block'; just killed a police detective and told himself he's done.

characters.name: Sally Reed
characters.line: Ambitious struggling actress and Barry's girlfriend, oblivious to his double life.

characters.name: Gene Cousineau
characters.line: Vain acting teacher who was dating Detective Moss when she vanished at his cabin.

characters.name: Monroe Fuches
characters.line: Barry's manipulative handler; forced out of LA after Barry butchered Goran to save him.

characters.name: NoHo Hank
characters.line: Cheerful Chechen lieutenant who has just taken over the outfit and struck an alliance with the Bolivians.

characters.name: Detective Janice Moss
characters.line: LAPD detective on the Ryan case; just shot dead by Barry after linking him to his marine crew.

beats.label: S2 · Gene keeps teaching
beats.text: Weeks after Moss vanishes, her case is closed for lack of leads; a grieving Gene nearly shuts the class down until Barry convinces him to keep teaching.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Anchors Barry's guilt-driven attachment to Gene — the relationship every later season is built on.

beats.label: S2 · Owing Hank one more
beats.text: Hank blackmails Barry into killing Burmese boss Esther; Barry can't go through with it and instead offers to train Hank's men to clear his debt.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the gang war that will collapse in the finale and defines Barry's inability to actually stop.

beats.label: S2 · Fuches turns informant
beats.text: Fuches is arrested in Cleveland after his DNA matches Goran's murder; Detective Loach flips him and sends him back to LA to elicit a confession from Barry.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Fuches's return to LA under coercion is the fuse that eventually detonates the Moss secret.

beats.label: S2 · Ronny and Lily
beats.text: Loach then blackmails Barry into killing his ex-wife's lover Ronny — a Taekwondo champion; the botched hit ends with both Ronny and Loach dead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The night Barry can't control the violence anymore — and the last obstacle to Fuches acting on his own.

beats.label: S2 · Fuches finds the body
beats.text: Barry cuts Fuches off for good; enraged, Fuches hunts through the woods around Gene's cabin and finds Moss's decomposing body in her hidden car.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The physical evidence that lets Fuches weaponise Moss's death against Barry from here on.

beats.label: S2 · Framing Gene
beats.text: Posing as a PI, Fuches lures Gene to Moss's body and calls in the murder as him; Fuches then flees, and Gene is arrested as the prime suspect in Moss's death.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Gene inside the Moss case as its suspect — the frame he spends every later season fighting.

beats.label: S2 · Massacre and memory
beats.text: Barry storms Hank's monastery hideout to reach Fuches, massacring nearly everyone inside; Fuches escapes, and that night Gene suddenly remembers: Barry killed Moss.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The knowledge that flips Gene's role in the show and sets Barry–Gene on the collision course of every season after.

cliffhanger.text: Gene is free but has just realised Barry murdered the woman he loved; Barry believes his monastery rampage has buried the secret for good.
questions: What will Gene do now that he knows Barry killed Moss?
Where does Fuches surface next, and what will he do to Barry?
Can Barry ever actually walk away from killing?

characters.name: Barry Berkman
characters.line: Failed to leave killing behind and just massacred a monastery to reach Fuches, believing his secret is safe.

characters.name: Sally Reed
characters.line: Rising actress whose breakthrough performance is built on a rewritten lie about her abusive ex-husband Sam.

characters.name: Gene Cousineau
characters.line: Just released from custody for Moss's murder; has suddenly recalled Fuches whispering that Barry killed her.

characters.name: Monroe Fuches
characters.line: Cast out by Barry, tried to frame Gene, escaped the monastery massacre, and is on the run out for revenge.

characters.name: NoHo Hank
characters.line: Chechen boss whose army was slaughtered but who is credited by his elders with killing Esther, keeping him in power.

characters.name: Cristobal Sifuentes
characters.line: Bolivian drug lord now allied with Hank and central to the LA peace.

beats.label: S3 · Back to the work
beats.text: Barry is back to contract killing found online; his relationship with Sally has curdled as she pours herself into a semi-autobiographical TV series.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets Barry's default state at season's open — killing again, isolated, resented — the trap the rest of the season springs.

beats.label: S3 · Kidnapping Gene
beats.text: Gene tries to kill Barry over Moss and fails; Barry kidnaps him and decides Gene can 'earn forgiveness' by taking acting work Barry coerces studios into offering.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's central engine — Barry weaponising Hollywood to force absolution — and the wedge that turns Gene into bait.

beats.label: S3 · Bombing Fernando
beats.text: Now openly in love with Cristobal, Hank pays Barry to bomb Cristobal's father-in-law Fernando; the hit lands but nearly kills Cristobal too.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Announces the Hank–Cristobal romance and the Bolivian retaliation that consumes their storyline this season.

beats.label: S3 · Fuches turns the families
beats.text: Back from hiding in Chechnya and posing as a PI, Fuches gives Barry's home address to the grieving families of his victims and sets them loose.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns Barry's past kills into a new pursuit — the biker attack and Sharon's poisoning both come out of this.

beats.label: S3 · Sally implodes
beats.text: Sally's show is cancelled and a viral meltdown at her former assistant ends her career; Barry's dark advice about revenge gets him kicked out.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Strips Sally of the identity that kept her tolerant of Barry — priming the break-up and her later flight.

beats.label: S3 · Hank rescues Cristobal
beats.text: Cristobal is kidnapped by his wife Elena and put through electroshock conversion therapy; Hank fights through a panther and a Bolivian dungeon to save him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The trauma that reshapes Hank into someone capable of the choices he'll make next season.

beats.label: S3 · Ambushed at last
beats.text: Sally kills a biker sent for Barry and flees while he takes the blame. Gene and Jim Moss then bait Barry to Jim's house, where police ambush and arrest him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's endpoint — Barry finally in cuffs for Moss, Sally on the run, the whole board in a new configuration.

cliffhanger.text: Barry is in police custody for Janice Moss's murder; Sally has fled to Missouri after killing a man; Hank has saved Cristobal but is deeply changed by what it cost him.
questions: Will Barry stand trial, or find another way out?
Can Sally live with what she did, alone and adrift?
What is left of Hank after what he did to survive Bolivia?

characters.name: Barry Berkman
characters.line: Just arrested for Janice Moss's murder after being lured into a trap by Gene and Jim Moss.

characters.name: Sally Reed
characters.line: Killed a biker in self-defence at Barry's apartment; Barry took the blame while she fled towards Missouri.

characters.name: Gene Cousineau
characters.line: Cooperated with Jim Moss to get Barry arrested; his public image half-rebuilt via a MasterClass deal.

characters.name: Monroe Fuches
characters.line: In prison after confessing to FBI agent Albert Nguyen that he was Barry's handler.

characters.name: NoHo Hank
characters.line: Traumatised after killing his way out of a Bolivian dungeon to rescue Cristobal.

characters.name: Cristobal Sifuentes
characters.line: Just freed from Elena's conversion therapy by Hank; back at his side but shaken.

characters.name: Jim Moss
characters.line: Janice's father, a menacing ex-Marine interrogator who engineered Barry's capture.

characters.name: Albert Nguyen
characters.line: Barry's old marine friend, now FBI, who once spared Barry and begged him to stop killing.

beats.label: S4 · Prison and press
beats.text: In prison, Fuches wears a wire for the FBI but Barry only apologises to him; Gene, publicly hailed a hero, agrees to a Vanity Fair profile against Jim's warnings.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Realigns the two men whose collision drives the finale — a chastened Fuches and a self-mythologising Gene.

beats.label: S4 · Escape from prison
beats.text: Barry offers to inform on Hank in exchange for witness protection; Fuches warns Hank, who sends assassins into the prison. Barry kills one and escapes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Barry back on the outside — the precondition for the time-jump and everything that follows.

beats.label: S4 · Hank buries his own
beats.text: To protect himself from the Chechen elders, Hank buries a room full of new associates in sand; Cristobal tries to leave and the Chechens kill him for it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The moral break in Hank — losing Cristobal to his own choice — that defines who he is for the rest of the show.

beats.label: S4 · Eight years gone
beats.text: Barry finds Sally at her apartment and they flee together. Eight years later they live in hiding as a married couple with a son, John, whom Barry has raised paranoid.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The time jump that resets the whole board — new geography, a child, and Sally trapped in a life she never chose.

beats.label: S4 · Gene resurfaces
beats.text: Bearded and disheveled after years in hiding in Israel, Gene resurfaces to sabotage a Barry biopic; hearing this, Barry decides to return to LA to kill him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The one event that pulls Barry off the mountain and back into the story's endgame.

beats.label: S4 · Bait and capture
beats.text: Hank kidnaps Sally and John to bait Barry; Barry is instead captured by Jim, who has convinced the DA that Gene manipulated Barry into killing Janice.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Fuses the two vendettas — Hank's and Jim's — into the single trap that forces the finale's confrontations.

beats.label: S4 · Gene shoots Barry
beats.text: Fuches shoots Hank at Nohobal and spares Barry's family. Barry surrenders at Gene's house — and Gene shoots him dead. A biopic later paints Barry a tragic hero, Gene the villain.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The series' ending: every relationship resolved, and the myth that survives Barry rewritten on screen for his son.

cliffhanger.text: Barry is dead by Gene's hand; Gene takes life in prison as the biopic rewrites the truth for John, who now sees his father as a hero.
questions: Does John's discovery of the truth ever pierce the myth the film sold him?
Can Sally build a life that isn't defined by Barry?
Who does history remember: the killer, or the villain the film invented?

characters.name: Barry Berkman
characters.line: Dead, shot by Gene in Gene's home moments after agreeing to turn himself in.

characters.name: Sally Reed
characters.line: Left Barry in the finale; now a distant high-school theatre teacher raising John alone.

characters.name: John
characters.line: Barry and Sally's teenage son, watching a whitewashed biopic that sells him a heroic father.

characters.name: Gene Cousineau
characters.line: Serving life in prison, publicly cast as the villain who orchestrated Janice's murder.

characters.name: Monroe Fuches
characters.line: Disappeared after killing Hank and sparing Barry's family — his final act of grace.

characters.name: NoHo Hank
characters.line: Dead at Nohobal, killed by Fuches after refusing to admit he caused Cristobal's death.

characters.name: Jim Moss
characters.line: Successfully framed Gene as the mastermind behind his daughter Janice's death.
